note: Adjudicated accidental variants: four of punctuation (one at the showing of the Host and one repeated in each of the three petitions) and one of orthography (the house i/j rule at w063). Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero divergence.

adjudicated.ruling: No comma after the second ecce, with handmissal-eo; witness do and the Ritus servandus print it. The relative clause is what the second ecce points at — behold Him who takes away — and cannot be cut loose from it.

Comma, with do and with the 1962 typical edition, which prints the petition this way. The corpus sets a colon at ordinarium.panem-caelestem w016, where both witnesses print one: the same sentence is pointed differently in the two places, and the edition follows each page rather than levelling them. The same ruling governs w034 and w051.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
